Whether actual period policy would have excluded Aug-26 products remains a genuine, separate, UNRESOLVED question - see target_recommendation.historical_event_pool_legality_status.
T1_through_T8_temporal_concepts.T8_community_retrospective_reference_dat: Where a community convention differs from the strict historical-event model - e.g. Edison's own T4 extending 16 days past its T3, per an established community format definition (EdisonFormat.com) rather than the tournament's own calendar. The Tokyo Dome candidate_pool's 'day before the event, matching the established community snapshot' framing (target_recommendation.event.pool_cutoff_reason, pre-session-7) is exactly a T8 claim about T4, not a claim about T3.

phase_b_model_a_and_b.method: Constructed hypothetical Format/Banlist/Pool dataclass instances directly in memory (retroformats.model), injected into a copy of the real Repository's dicts (never written to disk/data/), and ran the ACTUAL Validator._validate_format() against each. No canonical file was created.

model_a.validator_result: REJECTED. Finding: ERROR format.banlist-not-in-force - 'banlist ocg-test-hypothetical took effect 1999-08-26, after the snapshot date 1999-08-25'. Reproduced directly against retroformats.validate.Validator; exact error message quoted verbatim.

model_b.validator_result: ACCEPTED on this check. No banlist/region-related error or warning emitted - eff (1999-08-26) <= snapshot (1999-08-26) holds.

phase_b_model_a_and_b.semantic_coherence_of_model_b: Format schema's own text: period.snapshot 'usually is the date of the format's defining event.' Pool schema's own text: a pool represents cards 'legally available to players AT A FORMAT'S SNAPSHOT DATE.' Read naively, Model B (snapshot=08-26, pool.cutoff=08-25) LOOKS incoherent - the pool's own top-level description ties availability to the snapshot date, and Model B's pool cutoff is a day earlier than the snapshot. RESOLVED, not ignored: pool.schema.json's OWN legality_basis field exists precisely to license this - a pool's legality_basis licenses divergence from pure snapshot-date availability, per the schema's own words, and this repository's existing Edison pool already does exactly this (cutoff 16 days AFTER its own snapshot, not merely a day off, tagged legality_basis: 'community-retrospective'). CORRECTED 2026-08-30 (session 8): Model B is SEMANTICALLY COHERENT specifically under legality_basis: 'community-retrospective' (a modern community convention - the 'day before the event' cube tradition, matching card_pool.community_cross_check's ygoprodeck-tokyo-dome-cube source and this repository's own GOAT/Edison precedent - which the schema explicitly permits to deliberately differ from what was registerable at the historical event) - NOT under legality_basis: 'availability' (which would need the cutoff to track pure physical release timing) and NOT under legality_basis: 'historical-policy' either (an EARLIER version of this text wrongly claimed historical-policy, reasoning that 'day-of-event products were not legal in that day's tournament decks' per event_day_pool_interaction - but that source is ARCHIVED (superseded_findings), and even its own live text only establishes an absence of evidence for legality plus one card's [Gate Guardian's] incidental technical unusability, never a period-policy fact; historical-policy requires actual period-policy evidence for its exceptions, which this research chain does not have - see target_recommendation.historical_event_pool_legality_status, which remains UNRESOLVED for exactly this reason). Same-day tournament legality remaining genuinely UNKNOWN is preserved, not silently resolved: physical availability (a card existing on 08-26) != tournament legality (usable in an 08-26 deck) != community retrospective convention (the 'day before' cube tradition) - all three stay distinct propositions; the pool cutoff represents the THIRD one, by community convention, not a policy finding about the second.

phase_c_errata_recomputation_and_adjudic.errata_recomputation_method: Mechanically re-ran retroformats' real ErratumV2.selection_at() for all 296 errata in the live repo (not just the 6 pool-relevant ones) at BOTH date(1999,8,25) and date(1999,8,26), comparing each record's (chronology, candidate-events-tuple) result at the two dates. PROVENANCE NOTE: the specific set of '6 pool-relevant errata' (their IDs) was carried forward as the input list from superseded_findings.rejected_2026_08_rules_and_restriction_research.errata_intersection_audit - an ARCHIVED prior-session section, correctly not treated as live authoritative data on its own. This session did not re-derive pool membership from scratch (that would touch the protected 370-card pool's own computation, out of scope here); it used that archived list only as the candidate set to recompute selection_at() for, and separately re-ran selection_at() across the FULL live 296-erratum corpus (not just those 6) as an independent completeness check, which found the same result (zero changes) corpus-wide, not dependent on trusting the archived list's own membership claim.
phase_c_errata_recomputation_and_adjudic.errata_recomputation_result: 0 of 296 errata (including all 6 pool-relevant: erratum-castle-walls, erratum-cocoon-of-evolution, erratum-crush-card-virus, erratum-elegant-egotist, erratum-reinforcements, erratum-ultimate-offering) produce a different selection_at() result between 1999-08-25 and 1999-08-26. The 2 determinate records (crush-card-virus, reinforcements) resolve to the identical baseline ({}) events/coverage at both dates; the 4 ambiguous records remain ambiguous with the identical candidate sets at both dates. Moving the format snapshot by one day changes ZERO selected historical implementations, corpus-wide, not merely for the 6 pool-relevant records - checked exhaustively, not assumed.
phase_c_errata_recomputation_and_adjudic.pool_independence_confirmed: card_pool (the top-level packet field) already carries its OWN cutoff ('1999-08-25'), structurally independent of target_recommendation.snapshot - the two are already separate JSON fields, not one overloaded value; moving target_recommendation.snapshot does not touch card_pool.cutoff, the 370-card membership, or its digest at all.
phase_c_errata_recomputation_and_adjudic.adjudication: target_recommendation.snapshot MOVES from 1999-08-25 to 1999-08-26 (T3, the defining event date), matching schemas/format.schema.json's own stated convention ('usually the date of the format's defining event') and this repository's own direct Edison precedent (snapshot = 'the event the format is named for', independent of a differently-reasoned pool cutoff). card_pool.cutoff REMAINS 1999-08-25, unchanged, under an explicit legality_basis of 'community-retrospective' (CORRECTED 2026-08-30, session 8 - was wrongly recorded as 'historical-policy' here, citing the ARCHIVED event_day_pool_interaction finding as if it were a live period-tournament-policy fact; it is not - see target_recommendation.pool_legality_basis_recommendation and historical_event_pool_legality_status for the corrected reasoning and the still-UNRESOLVED, non-gating historical-policy question this replaces - not a pure availability derivation either - see T7/T8). This is SAFE per the errata recomputation (zero corpus-wide impact) and does not require re-deciding any of the 150 currently-ambiguous errata records. NOTHING in data/, formats/, or dist/ is touched - this is a research-packet metadata correction only, per explicit instruction not to materialize formats/1999-08-tokyo-dome/.
phase_c_errata_recomputation_and_adjudic.distinguishing_target_recommendation_fro: target_recommendation.snapshot (T3) is the CANONICAL HISTORICAL FORMAT's own reference date - now 1999-08-26, the event itself. card_pool.cutoff (T4/T8) is a SEPARATE, already-independent field that may legitimately remain 1999-08-25 under the 'day before the event' community-cube convention (T8) even though T3 correctly tracks the historical event date. These were never required to be equal, and keeping them distinct is the corrected model, not a compromise.

temporal_model_2026_08_30_session7.central_principle: A format's historical date, its card-pool cutoff, and a banlist's effective date are distinct facts unless the schema explicitly makes them equal. This repository's schema does not make them equal (T3 and T4 are separate fields; Edison's own precedent already diverges them substantially), and conflating them - as target_recommendation.snapshot's prior value implicitly did, by choosing a pool-cutoff-motivated date for what is documented and used as the format's own event-representative snapshot - was the actual root cause of the Aug-25/Aug-26 inconsistency external review found.

scope_class_status._resolved_class_note: RENAMED 2026-08-30 (session 9), from resolved_hypothesis: a real semantic bug this pass fixed - the old field/vocabulary (null | 'H1' | 'H2' | 'H3') let S1's own machine-readable value encode S2's answer (H2 vs H3), which is incoherent: a source can prove 'the restriction was tournament-specific' (S1's own proposition) without proving 'it was H2 rather than H3' (S2's proposition, a strictly NARROWER question S1 does not even ask). Under the old vocabulary, a PROVEN S1 was FORCED to also pick H2 or H3, so this exact legitimate state - S1 proven tournament-specific, S2 still genuinely undetermined - could not be honestly represented; a mutation test even had to construct the resulting contradiction (S1.resolved_hypothesis='H3' while tournament_extent_status.status stayed 'UNRESOLVED') to exercise the dependency check, without the packet's own model flagging that state as contradictory. CORRECTED: this field now carries ONLY the CLASS answer S1's own proposition actually asks - null while UNRESOLVED; 'H1_GENERAL_REGIONAL' only if general-regional policy is PROVEN; 'TOURNAMENT_SPECIFIC' if tournament-specific is PROVEN, WITHOUT choosing H2 or H3 - that choice belongs entirely to tournament_extent_status's own resolved_extent field (S2), which may legitimately remain null/UNRESOLVED even while this field is 'TOURNAMENT_SPECIFIC'. schema_representability_status may only reach its cleared status (RESOLVED_EXISTING_SCHEMA_SUFFICIENT) when this field is exactly 'H1_GENERAL_REGIONAL' - enforced mechanically in tests/test_yugi_kaiba_format_gate.py, not merely documented here. Central principle: a parent classification (S1: what CLASS of scope is this?) must not encode the answer to a child refinement (S2: IF tournament-specific, how far did it extend?) - those are independently representable states.
scope_class_status.proposition: S1 (scope CLASS, session 7 - corrects a session-6 conflation): was the three-card restriction a general OCG regional policy (H1), or a tournament/event-specific policy (H2 OR H3 - both are forms of tournament-specific policy per scope_hypotheses' own definitions: H2='Tokyo Dome/event-only list', H3='other tournament-specific scope'; NEITHER is 'general OCG list', which is H1 alone)? This is the proposition that determines whether an ordinary reusable region-scoped banlist object (schemas/banlist.schema.json) is a truthful data shape for this fact - see schema_representability_status, which is DERIVED from this axis, not from S2 below. ADDED 2026-08-30 (session 8): tournament_extent_status (S2)'s own blocking_role is ALSO now derived from this axis (NOT_APPLICABLE if this resolves H1; NON_BLOCKING_FOR_TARGET_ARTIFACT if this resolves tournament-specific) - S1 is now the single driver both axes downstream of it depend on.
scope_class_status.current_evidentiary_lean: AGAINST H1, though not formally PROVEN: three converging sources (Master Guide's '大会限定' header, the V Jump image's event-name-tied '「決闘者伝説」では', home.att.ne.jp's '１回目の大会（東京ドーム）'用に発表された制限') all use tournament-scoped language, none uses general-regional language - see target_event_applicability_status.what_is_well_supported for the full citation. This makes H1 well-evidenced-against, but S1 remains UNRESOLVED in the strict sense: no source explicitly and affirmatively DENIES general applicability, and this research chain has not personally inspected a primary document that settles the question either way.

tournament_extent_status._resolved_extent_note_2026_08_30_session: ADDED (session 9): S2's own machine-readable resolved value - null while UNRESOLVED; 'H2' or 'H3' once PROVEN. Previously S2 had a status word (UNRESOLVED/PROVEN) but no separate value field of its own, and scope_class_status.resolved_hypothesis was wrongly overloaded to carry BOTH S1's class answer and S2's H2-vs-H3 answer in one field - forcing a PROVEN S1 to also pick H2 or H3, which made the perfectly legitimate state 'S1 proven tournament-specific, S2 genuinely still undetermined' inexpressible without an internal contradiction. This field and scope_class_status.resolved_class are now fully independent: status='PROVEN' with resolved_extent=null, or status='UNRESOLVED' with resolved_extent non-null, are each individually contradictory (mechanically rejected - see tests/test_yugi_kaiba_format_gate.py), but S2's status/resolved_extent pair as a WHOLE is never required to be consistent with S1's resolved_class beyond blocking_role's own state machine below.
tournament_extent_status._correction_note_2026_08_30_session8: Session 7 kept this axis (S2) inside canonicalization_status.load_bearing_axes unconditionally, justified only as 'historical completeness' - internally inconsistent (it was simultaneously described as NOT independently load-bearing in canonicalization_status.reasoning) and logically broken on the H1 branch: if scope_class_status (S1) resolves to H1 (general-regional policy), S2's own premise - that the restriction was tournament-specific - is FALSE, so S2 cannot coherently be required to reach PROVEN under that branch. Re-derived from scratch, independently cross-checked before implementation: blocking_role below is now an explicit, DERIVED/CONDITIONAL classification (matching schema_representability_status's own pattern), not a flat load-bearing membership. See canonicalization_status.conditionally_tracked_axes for where this is now declared (moved OUT of load_bearing_axes).
tournament_extent_status.proposition: S2 (tournament EXTENT, session 7 - split out from the old outer_scope_status): GIVEN S1 resolves to tournament-specific (or pending that resolution), did the restriction apply only to the August 26 finals (H2), or to the full qualifier+finals tournament programme / another explicitly-bounded population (H3)? A REFINEMENT of S1, not a substitute for it - do not let S2 masquerade as S1: proving H3 over H2 does NOT establish general-regional policy (H1); it only widens which PART of the tournament series was covered, while remaining tournament-specific throughout.

state_machine.if_scope_class_status_unresolved: S2's own applicability is itself pending S1's resolution - a live, valuable, but non-gating historical research question. blocking_role.current_value = 'CONDITIONAL_PENDING_S1'.
state_machine.if_scope_class_status_resolves_general_r: (scope_class_status.resolved_class = 'H1_GENERAL_REGIONAL') S2's premise (that the restriction was tournament-specific) is FALSE - a general-regional policy applies regardless of which tournament population would otherwise be in question, so the finals-vs-qualifiers distinction dissolves entirely. blocking_role.current_value = 'NOT_APPLICABLE'. MUST NOT block canonicalization under this branch - requiring a false premise's refinement to resolve would be incoherent.
state_machine.if_scope_class_status_resolves_tournamen: (scope_class_status.resolved_class = 'TOURNAMENT_SPECIFIC' - this branch does NOT require S2's own resolved_extent to be H2, H3, or anything at all; S2 may legitimately remain status='UNRESOLVED'/resolved_extent=null here, and that is now a fully coherent state, not a contradiction) S2 becomes a live, applicable historical question, but remains NON-BLOCKING for THIS target artifact specifically - NOT because H2/H3 logically entail Aug-26-event coverage by themselves (CORRECTED 2026-08-30, adversarial review: this axis's own proposition defines H3 disjunctively - 'the full qualifier+finals tournament programme / another explicitly-bounded population' - and an earlier version of this branch's text silently dropped the second disjunct, which is not textually guaranteed to include the finals; do not overclaim logical entailment H3's label does not actually supply), but because a SEPARATE, independently load-bearing axis already gates that specific fact: target_event_applicability_status's own proposition IS 'restriction in force AT the Aug-26 target event', and it must independently reach PROVEN regardless of how S2 resolves (see canonicalization_status.load_bearing_axes). target_recommendation.event scopes the artifact ('1999-08-tokyo-dome') narrowly to the single 1999-08-26 Tokyo Dome event, not to a wider tournament season, and target_event_applicability_status is what proves the restriction actually applied there - S2 (H2-vs-H3) only ever refines what ELSE, beyond that already-gated fact, the restriction covered. Applying this research chain's own established central rule (restriction_list_current._read_me_first: 'a historical uncertainty is a canonicalization blocker only if resolving it could change a historical fact ASSERTED OR IMPLIED by the canonical artifact') to S2 specifically (not to the S1 question session 6 actually tested when it restored the old bundled outer_scope_status axis - see _correction_note above): resolving H2-vs-H3 would NOT change what this narrowly Aug-26-event-scoped artifact asserts or implies (that fact is target_event_applicability_status's job, tracked and gated independently), only what ELSE the restriction is known to have covered. It WOULD matter for a DIFFERENT, more broadly-scoped hypothetical future artifact (one claiming coverage of the qualifying rounds too) - but that is not the artifact this research chain is targeting. If a future finding somehow established the restriction did NOT apply at the finals specifically (an exotic reading of H3's second disjunct), that would falsify target_event_applicability_status directly, not merely 'resolve S2' - the framework already has room for that outcome via the independent axis, it does not depend on this branch's own reasoning holding up. blocking_role.current_value = 'NON_BLOCKING_FOR_TARGET_ARTIFACT'.

blocking_role.current_state: scope_class_status.status = UNRESOLVED, resolved_class = null (neither H1_GENERAL_REGIONAL nor TOURNAMENT_SPECIFIC formally proven yet). Per the state machine's first branch: S2's own applicability is itself pending S1. NOT yet classified NOT_APPLICABLE or NON_BLOCKING_FOR_TARGET_ARTIFACT - both require S1 to actually resolve first. In EITHER eventual S1 outcome, S2 does not block canonicalization of the target artifact (1999-08-tokyo-dome) - it is either moot (general-regional) or non-blocking-but-tracked (tournament-specific) - so S2's own UNRESOLVED status does not itself withhold canonicalization readiness; the six independent load-bearing axes and the derived schema_representability_status axis are what currently keep canonicalization_status at UNRESOLVED_BLOCKING, not this axis. This axis's own resolved_extent also remains null, consistently with status=UNRESOLVED.
blocking_role.not_a_reversion_to_session_5: Session 5's rejected test asked whether resolving an axis would change GENERATED BYTES - a mechanical-output test session 6 correctly rejected as insufficient (a fact can be irrelevant to generated bytes and still be essential to historical truth). This derivation does NOT use that test. It applies session 6's own CORRECTED replacement test (asserted-or-implied-fact) to S2 in isolation, for the first time - S1 and S2 were bundled together as one field (the original outer_scope_status) until session 7 split them, and when session 6 ran the corrected test on that bundled axis, its actual justification (quoted in canonicalization_dependency_note below) was substantively about S1 (would an ordinary region-scoped banlist object misrepresent a one-event rule as general policy), not a genuine test of S2 (finals vs. wider tournament population) on its own terms. This is the first time the corrected test has actually been run against S2 specifically - independently cross-checked before implementation, not asserted unilaterally.
blocking_role.canonicalization_dependency_note: Session 6's own restoration text (docs/research/yugi-kaiba-format-source-gate.md, 'Phase C: outer scope (H2-vs-H3)'): 'If H2 is true... encoding it as an ordinary data/banlists/ocg/1999-08.json would... assert this was the OCG region's general policy' vs 'If H3 is true (a genuinely broader... regional policy, closer in kind to how GOAT/Edison/Tengu are already modeled), representing it as an ordinary region-scoped banlist would be comparatively defensible' - this is the H3-as-H1 conflation session 7 already found and fixed for schema_representability_status (see that axis's own _correction_note_2026_08_30_session7). The SAME conflation is what made S2 look load-bearing here too: the actual concern in that quoted text is S1-shaped (general-regional vs event-specific), mislabeled onto H2-vs-H3.

tournament_extent_status.what_remains_unresolved: The EXACT scope boundary - H2 (the August 26 Tokyo Dome FINALS specifically) versus H3 (the whole national tournament run, including qualifying rounds before the finals) - is not pinned down and different sources lean different ways. REVISED 2026-08-30 after adversarial review and personal re-examination of the page image: the V Jump intro sentence '大会は使用Cの枚数制限などがあるので' (the tournament has card usage-count restrictions, etc.) sits ABOVE and visually introduces BOTH the match-conditions box (deck 40+, side deck 10) AND the restricted-card box on the same two-box spread; its exact phrase '枚数制限' textually echoes the restricted-card box's own heading '使用枚数が制限されたカードたち' far more closely than it echoes the match-conditions box's plain count statements ('デッキは40枚以上', 'サイドデッキは10枚'), which never use the word '制限' at all - so, on vocabulary alone, this sentence more plausibly refers ahead to the 3-card restriction than to deck-size rules. HOWEVER, even under that reading, the sentence only proves the restriction was being PUBLICLY DISCUSSED while qualifiers were running ('予選のまっただ中') - it does not say the restriction APPLIED to qualifying matches themselves, as opposed to being advance notice for an eventual finals-only rule. 'Discussed during qualifiers' and 'in effect during qualifiers' are different propositions, and only the former is textually supported. Master Guide's header, by contrast, explicitly attaches '大会限定' to the single August 26 date (H2-leaning). Net effect of this revision: the H3 lean recorded in scope_hypotheses after the initial reading ("the strongest concrete lean toward H3 found in this research chain") overclaimed and has been walked back to genuinely UNRESOLVED - H2 and H3 remain live, roughly evenly-supported alternatives, not H3-favored. Per this pass's explicit instruction: this tension is recorded, not force-reconciled.

event_disruption_reassessment.confidence_reasoning: Convergent, mutually-corroborating detail across multiple independently-authored retrospective sources (several read directly in full by the research swarm): specific attendance figures (~55,000 admitted, ~10,000+ turned away, against ~50,000 capacity), a named cancelled product (Premium Pack (Japanese) sales suspended after ~2 hours then cancelled outright - independently corroborated by the adjudicator's own read of yugioh-history.com's 1999 summary page, which states plainly the venue-exclusive pack's sales were halted 'due to congestion'), riot police deployment, and a Konami apology.
event_disruption_reassessment.period_source_status: NO PERIOD (1999) ARTICLE OBTAINED OR PERSONALLY INSPECTED. Several of the most specialized candidate sources (ygoldschool.com, silent-night.jp, aoiblog.online) returned DNS-resolution failures or TLS certificate mismatches consistently across every fetch attempt in this sandboxed environment, across both research sessions. This is reported as a tooling limitation, not evidence of anything.
event_disruption_reassessment.tournament_completion_status: NOT PRIMARY-SOURCE PROVEN. A directly-fetched retrospective (game-blog.net) states the finals were never held and prize distribution could not be completed, but this rests on the same evidence tier as the rest of this finding (retrospective, not contemporaneous) - do not elevate this to a stronger label than the tier it actually rests on.
event_disruption_reassessment.admission_policy_note: One weakly-sourced but specific claim (reached only via WebSearch synthesis of a blog that could not be directly fetched) suggests admission was broadened shortly before the event from 'qualifying-tournament participants only' to 'anyone bringing a copy of Weekly Shonen Jump magazine' - which, if true, would mean Tokyo Dome did not cleanly inherit a closed qualifier-only structure and directly contributed to the overcrowding. Rated AMBIGUOUS, single-sourced, not independently confirmed.

tokyo_dome_rule_profile_readiness.derived_from: authoritative_rule_matrix (primary_source_resolution_2026_08_29.three_column_evidence_matrix), recomputed live from that matrix during 2026-08-29 consolidation - not a separately-maintained truth table.
tokyo_dome_rule_profile_readiness.explanation: Recomputed directly from the 21-row authoritative matrix: every single row's tokyo_dome.status is UNKNOWN (21 of 21 rows). This is true even though the primary-source discovery (the actual 1999 Expert Rules guide) substantially strengthened several rows at the starter_box and later_pre_tokyo_dome tiers - the guide directly documents Expert Rules content, but its own text explicitly frames tournament adoption as a possibility ('may possibly adopt'), not a certainty, and no source anywhere in this research chain establishes which ruleset Tokyo Dome itself used. A rule being proven at the Starter Box or later_pre_tokyo_dome tier does NOT prove it was the rule at Tokyo Dome specifically. This pass has not manufactured Tokyo-Dome-tier evidence where none exists. A canonical Tokyo Dome rule profile cannot be responsibly proposed while its own event-tier column is this empty, regardless of how well-resolved the other two tiers have become.
tokyo_dome_rule_profile_readiness.what_would_unblock_this: A genuinely event-specific source (an actual Tokyo Dome tournament rule sheet, organizer announcement, or contemporaneous 1999 press coverage of the tournament's mechanics) naming which ruleset was used - not another retrospective inferring event rules from general OCG timing, and not the guide's own 'tournaments may adopt' hedge treated as if it were a certainty.

primary_source_resolution_2026_08_29.method: Four independent evidence lanes were kept separate: restriction-list provenance, contemporaneous Expert Rules materials, Tokyo Dome event documentation, and adversarial provenance audit. The final adjudicator personally inspected the load-bearing source objects and did not promote a claim because multiple agents or websites repeated it.
primary_source_resolution_2026_08_29.source_promotion_invariant: A Tokyo-Dome-specific cell may be PROVEN only when its source_ids include an inspected source that establishes the event-specific proposition. A calendar date may be PROVEN as a rule-effective transition only when a source establishes the transition; publication or product date alone is insufficient.

document.title: 遊戯王 オフィシャルカード デュエルモンスターズ 公式ガイドスターターブック
document.english_title: Yu-Gi-Oh! Official Card Duel Monsters Official Guide Starter Book
document.edition: Edition/printing not independently established from the scan metadata
document.scan_provenance: Internet Archive item metadata identifies the period title/date, uploader, 600 ppi OCR/scan files, and a 2025 public date. The repository does not own the scan and no scan pages are committed.
document.authenticity_confidence: The inspected images are scans of a period Japanese guide bearing the Shueisha/Studio Hard title and page sequence. Publisher/edition provenance is strong for the object; the hosting upload is a later archival copy, not a contemporaneous web publication.

direct_findings.pages: 107-108 (title page p.107 + continuation p.108; see correction note in 'establishes')
direct_findings.section: 第3章 エキスパートルール / Expert Rule
direct_findings.excerpt: 上級デュエリストのためにコナミが用意した特別ルール。ノーマルルールに比べより、戦略的駆け引きが高められている。大会などではこのルールを採用する可能性もあるので、挑戦して損はないだろう。(p.107) ... 通常の公式ルールじゃ飽き足りないデュエリストにオススメ!! ちょっとハイレベルなルールを加えた「エキスパートルール」を紹介するぞ。基本的なルールは公式ルールと同様だが、「エキスパートルール」では新たに3つのルールが加わっており(p.108)
direct_findings.translation: Expert Rules are presented (on the chapter's title page, p.107) as a special rule Konami prepared for advanced duelists, with more elevated strategic play, and a note that tournaments may possibly adopt this rule; the continuation (p.108) recommends it to duelists who find the normal official rules insufficient and states three rules are added to the basic official rules, which remain otherwise the same as normal.
direct_findings.establishes: Expert Rules were documented in this guide by its 1999-05-05 publication; the text does not identify a universal effective date or say that Tokyo Dome adopted them. CORRECTED THIS SESSION: the excerpt above splices two adjacent but distinct print pages (the chapter's title page, p.107, carrying the tournament-adoption sentence; and its body continuation, p.108) - the original commit's excerpt merged them with an ellipsis in a way that could read as one continuous passage. Personally re-verified against the archive.org page images directly (leaf n106 = printed p.107, leaf n107 = printed p.108) by the adjudicator this session.

direct_findings.section: ルール1 魔法カードの連続使用OK / Rule 1
direct_findings.excerpt: 公式ルールでは魔法カードはターン中に1枚しか場に出せなかった。しかし「エキスパートルール」では ... 手札にある限り、何枚でも使用することができる
direct_findings.translation: Under the official rules only one Magic card could be put on the field during a turn; under Expert Rules, any number of Magic cards may be used during the player's turn while in hand, subject to the five-card field limit.
direct_findings.establishes: The guide's Expert Rules text describes the activation-cap change; it does not prove the date on which ordinary OCG play or Tokyo Dome changed to it.

direct_findings.section: ルール2 強力なモンスターには触媒が必須 / Rule 2
direct_findings.excerpt: エキスパートルールでは ... レベル5～6のモンスターなら1体、レベル7以上のモンスターなら2体を墓地へ送らなければならない
direct_findings.translation: Under Expert Rules, a Level 5–6 monster requires one monster sent from the field to the Graveyard and a Level 7 or higher monster requires two.
direct_findings.establishes: The level-based Tribute requirement is directly present in the 1999 guide's Expert Rules section; it does not prove Tokyo Dome used the section.

direct_findings.section: ルール3 融合は手札の中でOK / Rule 3
direct_findings.excerpt: 公式ルールでは「融合」カードが手札にあり、融合素材モンスター2体さえ揃えば融合が行えなかった。しかし「エキスパートルール」では ... 手札に1体と「融合」カードでも融合が行える
direct_findings.translation: Under the official rules Fusion could not be performed merely with Polymerization and two materials in hand; under Expert Rules, Fusion may be performed with material in hand.
direct_findings.establishes: Hand-based Fusion materials are directly described in the guide; the text does not establish the date or event of adoption.

effective_date_adjudication._naming_note: Field names below are deliberately explicit about WHAT is proven, per task guidance to avoid ambiguous names like 'expert_rules_available_by_1999_05_05' that could be misread normatively (as if 'available' meant 'in force'). Three genuinely distinct propositions, three distinct fields.

guide_publication_date.reason: The scan is dated 1999-05-05 and the catalogue record independently lists the same release date.

rules_documented_by_date.reason: The inspected pages (personally re-verified this session via direct archive.org page-image fetch, not merely cited) are an Expert Rules chapter in the dated guide, directly documenting all three rule changes (repeated Magic-card use, Level-based Tribute cost, hand-based Fusion materials). This proves the RULES ARE DOCUMENTED by 1999-05-05 - it does not by itself prove any of those rules were the NORMATIVE OCG rule as of that date; see normative_effective_date_status below.

normative_effective_date_status.reason: The primary guide documents the rules but its wording does not say they became effective that day; the exact date remains a secondary reconstruction.

tokyo_dome_event_ruleset_adjudication.negative_result: CORRECTED 2026-08-30 (session 11): this field previously read event_specific_source_ids_inspected: [] and claimed no inspectable source was located - that was already stale the moment it was written, since contemporaneous_source_investigation_2026_08_30 (a later pass the same day) personally inspected a page image attributed to V Jump 1999-09 that directly states, in its own words, "採用ルールは「エキスパートルール」" ("The adopted rule is 'Expert Rules'") inside a feature specifically about the target event (決闘者伝説/Duelist Legend). That statement was never propagated into this field until now. Corrected: this source IS event-specific in its own subject matter (unlike the Official Guide Starter Book, which never names Tokyo Dome), and its wording is an unhedged assertion, not a hedged possibility like the Starter Book's own 採用する可能性もある language. However, per source_authentication_status, this source itself remains SUPPORTED_BUT_INCOMPLETE, not PROVEN - it is single-hosted (ygoldschool.com only), with no independently-verified chain of custody from the physical 1999 magazine to this image, despite an exhaustive session-11 search (see tokyo_dome_vjump_page20_authentication_hunt_2026_08_30_session11) that located no independent copy via any of the channels searched. An unauthenticated source's unhedged wording does not, by itself, clear this project's verified-source bar for an event-specific ruleset claim, so status correctly remains UNKNOWN rather than being promoted. Separately (session 11, genuinely new this pass): photographs (EXIF-consistent with an original capture) of a document purporting to be a 1999 Konami invitation and tournament rulebook for this exact event were located (source_id daiti0526-tokyo-dome-invitation-and-dm2-rulebook-2018) - but it governs a DIFFERENT, parallel competition track (the Game Boy Color "Duel Monsters II: Dark Duel Stories" video-game tournament, with its own separate cards-you-cannot-use list keyed by in-game card number) and never mentions Expert Rules or the tabletop OCG ruleset at all. It is recorded here only so a future researcher does not mistake its video-game-specific rules for OCG event rules - not as OCG ruleset evidence.
tokyo_dome_event_ruleset_adjudication.event_disruption_relevance: The period reporting confirms severe event disruption but does not establish whether an OCG competition ran normally, which stages existed, or whether any rule tier was applied. No clean event rules inference is permitted.
tokyo_dome_event_ruleset_adjudication.what_would_close_it: A Tokyo Dome 1999 official programme/rule sheet, qualifier invitation or entry regulation, or period Japanese magazine/newspaper report that names the tabletop OCG rules or restriction list - or independent authentication of the already-inspected V Jump 1999-09 source itself (see source_authentication_status).

engine_reassessment.current_behavior: Pinned ocgcore's field::calculate_battle_damage reproduces the historical ATK-vs-ATK and ATK-vs-DEF result table, including the attacker-recoil outcome, as its default behavior with no flag or card script required (aside from the separately-tracked 0-ATK-tie exception, DUEL_0_ATK_DESTROYED). Personally verified 2026-08-29 (session 3) against the exact pinned EDOPro ocgcore revision (edo9300/ygopro-core commit 158aebe758be3c46249c75d602e3f16d63d2ef31, per docs/research/ocgcore-flags.md), field::calculate_battle_damage in processor.cpp (lines 2929-3252 at that revision), fetched directly from GitHub. For every historical outcome (ATK>ATK, ATK=ATK non-zero, ATK<ATK, ATK>DEF, ATK=DEF, ATK<DEF, direct attack), the pinned engine's DEFAULT behavior (no flags, no card scripts) matches the 1999 rulebook and the 1999-05-05 guide exactly, including the ATK<ATK and ATK<DEF 'attacker recoil' lines the task specifically pointed to (damp = pa; core.battle_damage[damp] = d - a; at both processor.cpp:2965-2966 and processor.cpp:3122-3123). The sole exception is the already-separately-tracked 0-ATK-vs-0-ATK tie (DUEL_0_ATK_DESTROYED - default is neither destroyed; flag restores the 1999 rulebook's literal 'even 0=0 destroys both' wording). Independently cross-checked against Yugipedia's current official damage-calculation rules table (action=parse&page=Damage_calculation via the MediaWiki API, since the article page itself 403s), which states the identical result table as CURRENT official Yu-Gi-Oh! rules - DEF-ATK 'attacker recoil' damage is not a retro-only mechanic, it is the unbroken modern rule. The arithmetic/destruction table is therefore ENGINE-REPRESENTABLE BY DEFAULT, not a blocker, regardless of how strong the historical continuity evidence is.

engine_representation_blockers.definition: Historical behavior established well enough to identify, independent of Tokyo-Dome-specific enforcement evidence, but not representable by the current engine. UPDATED 2026-08-29 (session 3): the standard is no longer 'PROVEN at Starter Box + no located evidence of change' (that is source-silence reasoning and was already correctly rejected for chain_spell_speed_priority). The current standard requires BOTH: (a) a matrix row's starter_box.status == PROVEN, and EITHER its tokyo_dome.status == PROVEN or a positive_continuity_evidence entry flagged not_silence_based (a second, independently-dated primary source that AFFIRMATIVELY restates the rule, not merely an absence of a documented change) - the historical-applicability half; AND (b) an actually-demonstrated engine_reassessment classification of NOT_REPRESENTABLE - the engine-incompatibility half, which must itself be evidenced (source-code inspection or equivalent), not assumed merely because a rule is old. Positive historical continuity alone (a) does not create a blocker without (b): battle_calculation was removed from this list this session after personally inspecting the pinned ocgcore source and finding its arithmetic/destruction table already matches the historical rule by default - see engine_reassessment.battle_calculation and positive_continuity_evidence.items.battle_calculation.
items: deck_out - LP-comparison outcome on empty-deck draw failure, PROVEN at Starter Box tier, and independently re-documented (not a silence-based inference) in the same guide (same publication date as the Expert Rules chapter) that documents Expert Rules (which does not touch this rule) - a second, dated, positive primary source ~113 days before Tokyo Dome, not a silence-based inference. No DUEL_* flag or OCG_Player field can substitute it. See positive_continuity_evidence.items.deck_out for the full evidentiary chain, including externally-corroborated evidence that the actual change occurred ~8 months AFTER Tokyo Dome (2000-04-20, 'New Expert Rule'/Magic Ruler).

architecture_verdict_detail.explicitly_not_counted_as_a_blocker: REVISED this session: chain_spell_speed_priority is explicitly NOT counted as an independent blocker. The prior pass had treated 'no chain/Spell-Speed concept' as PROVEN at the Starter Box tier from the same source's silence on the topic - the primary-source discovery's own more careful redo correctly reclassifies this as UNKNOWN (silence is not proof of absence), so there is no longer a secure historical basis for treating the full chain/priority model as an unconditional engine gap; only the narrower, genuinely PROVEN trap_activation_frequency fact above is retained as a blocker. tribute_summon and fusion_material_location are also explicitly NOT counted as independent blockers, per the task's own guidance: 'Do not classify an engine mismatch as a Tokyo Dome blocker if the relevant historical rule's applicability to Tokyo Dome is itself unknown.' Both are now PROVEN as DOCUMENTED in the 1999 Expert Rules guide (later_pre_tokyo_dome tier), and the modern engine default already matches that documented Expert-Rules state - so if that state turns out to be what Tokyo Dome used, there is no engine gap at all; the only open question is event adoption, which is a historical blocker already counted above, not a second engine blocker. ADDED 2026-08-29 (session 3): battle_calculation's arithmetic/destruction table is also explicitly NOT counted as an independent blocker, for a THIRD, distinct reason from the two above - not because Tokyo-Dome applicability is unknown (its historical continuity evidence is actually strong, see positive_continuity_evidence.items.battle_calculation), but because personal inspection of the pinned ocgcore source (processor.cpp field::calculate_battle_damage, revision 158aebe758be3c46249c75d602e3f16d63d2ef31) found the engine already reproduces the historical ATK<ATK/ATK<DEF attacker-recoil result as its default behavior - there is no engine mismatch to block on. A separate, historically UNKNOWN question (whether a distinctive damage-step timing/response-window procedure existed) was considered and explicitly NOT used to manufacture a blocker from an unproven historical claim - see engine_reassessment.battle_calculation and the mutation tests guarding against exactly this move.
architecture_verdict_detail.conclusion: Both blocker categories are independently sufficient on their own; together they justify BLOCKED_BY_BOTH. This is NOT the same reasoning as before the primary-source discovery even though the label is unchanged: the discovery meaningfully shrank the historical-evidence blockers (Expert Rules content is now documented, not merely secondary-reconstructed) and meaningfully shrank the engine blockers (chain/priority downgraded from unconditional to not-counted; tribute/fusion confirmed not to be blockers at all) - but it did not resolve either category to zero. Even a hypothetical future discovery of a primary 1999 Tokyo Dome tournament rule sheet (resolving every historical-evidence blocker) would still leave deck-out and the narrow Trap-only Battle-Phase timing rule unrepresentable by current engine architecture without a runtime change, which this pass does not propose or make. UPDATED 2026-08-29 (session 3): the battle-calculation recoil quirk is REMOVED from this list - personal inspection of the pinned ocgcore source found it is already engine-representable by default, so it would not remain unrepresentable even in that hypothetical; see engine_reassessment.battle_calculation.

positive_continuity_evidence._read_me_first: This structure exists to draw the exact distinction this session's task required: 'PROVEN at Starter Box + no located evidence of change' (source silence, NOT sufficient on its own to promote a rule to an unconditional Tokyo Dome engine blocker) versus 'PROVEN at Starter Box + independently PROVEN restated in a second, dated, primary source close to the event' (positive persistence evidence, which legitimately can). Every item below requires an independently-dated primary or tier-1/2 source that AFFIRMATIVELY documents the rule as still in effect - not merely a lack of a documented change. chain_spell_speed_priority deliberately has NO entry here: no second dated source was found restating (or changing) it, so its continuity remains genuinely unknown, not merely under-evidenced silence being mistaken for proof.
positive_continuity_evidence.standard: An item here satisfies only the HISTORICAL-APPLICABILITY half of the unconditional-engine-blocker standard. Combined with a matrix row's starter_box.status == PROVEN AND an engine classification of NOT_REPRESENTABLE (the separately-evidenced ENGINE-INCOMPATIBILITY half - not assumed, not inferred from a rule being old), the two together are sufficient for the standard even though the matrix's own tokyo_dome.status column correctly remains UNKNOWN (no event-specific source exists). The two are not in tension: tokyo_dome.status answers 'does a Tokyo-Dome-specific document exist' (no); this structure answers 'is there a narrower, dated, evidence-backed reason to believe the rule still applied 113 days later regardless' (yes, for all three items here). UPDATED 2026-08-29 (session 3): having an item HERE does NOT by itself make a rule area a blocker - battle_calculation is a live counter-example: its historical continuity evidence is exactly as strong as deck_out's and trap_activation_frequency's, but personal inspection of the pinned ocgcore source found no engine mismatch, so it is NOT in engine_representation_blockers.items despite remaining in this structure. See arithmetic_vs_timing_split on that item for the full adjudication.

deck_out.mechanism: independently-dated intermediate primary source, not source silence
deck_out.intermediate_source_quote_translated: '...if either the player's or the opponent's deck runs out first, and either side becomes unable to draw a card, the outcome is decided by the difference in Life Points between the two. In that case, whichever side has more Life Points at the moment the deck ran out is the winner.' (printed p.105, personally verified against the page image 2026-08-29)
deck_out.expert_rules_relationship: Expert Rules (same publication, pp.107-109) documents exactly three changes - Tribute Summon, removal of the one-Spell/one-Trap-per-turn activation cap, and hand-based Fusion materials. Deck-out is not among them; the Official Rule Reference chapter (this quote) is the standing rule Expert Rules layers on top of, unchanged.
deck_out.upper_bound_evidence: Independent, non-primary corroboration (NOT personally inspected at root - see sources.deck-out-history.reliability_note): the Japanese Yu-Gi-Oh Wiki (yugioh-wiki.net, 3 separate pages) and yugioh-history.com (independently authored, no cross-citation) agree the LP-comparison rule held until the 'New Expert Rule' accompanying Magic Ruler's release, 2000-04-20 - about 8 months AFTER Tokyo Dome. One wiki page cites this to a print rule card packaged with Booster R1. A competing claim (a 2024 tweet by manga staff member Ito Akira, personally verified accessible and quoted 2026-08-29 via mirror) recalls the rule as a 'draw' rather than LP-comparison - this directly contradicts BOTH personally-inspected primary documents (Starter Box rulebook AND this May 1999 guide) and is assessed as an unreliable decades-later recollection, not evidence against continuity; even the source that quoted the tweet ultimately sided with the LP-comparison rulebook text once checked.

trap_activation_frequency.mechanism: independently-dated intermediate primary source, not source silence
trap_activation_frequency.intermediate_source_quote_translated: '...during the Battle Phase, you cannot use Magic Cards other than Trap Cards that are on the field.' (printed p.104, personally verified against the page image 2026-08-29) - textually identical to the Starter Box rulebook's 'Spell Cards placed on the field other than Trap Cards cannot be used during the Battle Phase.'
trap_activation_frequency.expert_rules_relationship: Expert Rules removes only the one-Spell/one-Trap-PER-TURN activation cap (any number of Magic cards may be used per turn, field-limited) - a DIFFERENT axis from which card TYPES may be used during the Battle Phase specifically. The Battle-Phase Trap-only restriction is not among Expert Rules' three documented changes.
trap_activation_frequency.upper_bound_evidence: Officially documented upper bound: Quick-Play Spell Cards (速攻魔法), the first OCG mechanism permitting a Spell/Magic Card to be used during the Battle Phase, were introduced in the 'Magic Ruler' booster, confirmed via Konami's own Yu-Gi-Oh! Neuron card database listing (release date 2000-04-20) - about 8 months AFTER Tokyo Dome.

battle_calculation.mechanism: independently-dated intermediate primary source, not source silence
battle_calculation.intermediate_source_quote_translated: '...if the attacking player's monster's ATK is lower than the ATK/DEF of the attacked enemy monster, [the attacker is destroyed / neither is destroyed]; the value obtained by subtracting the attacking monster's ATK from the enemy's [ATK/DEF] is deducted from the ATTACKING PLAYER's Life Points.' (printed pp.103-104, personally verified against the page image 2026-08-29) - textually identical to the Starter Box rulebook's battle-damage procedure.
battle_calculation.expert_rules_relationship: Expert Rules does not mention battle damage or the Damage determination procedure at all; this guide's own Official Rule Reference chapter (this quote) is presented as the unmodified, standing rule.
battle_calculation.upper_bound_evidence: No source found (2026-08-29 research sweep) documents the ATK-vs-ATK/ATK-vs-DEF recoil-damage ARITHMETIC ever changing; what is documented is a later formalization of Damage Step TIMING/response windows (Master Rule 3, 2014-03-21) around the same arithmetic - a different axis from the result table itself. RESOLVED 2026-08-29 (session 3): the adversarial engine-representability caveat previously recorded here was investigated by personally fetching and inspecting the exact pinned ocgcore revision's source (edo9300/ygopro-core commit 158aebe758be3c46249c75d602e3f16d63d2ef31, processor.cpp field::calculate_battle_damage) - the recoil arithmetic DOES already match modern rules and the pinned engine's default behavior exactly. See arithmetic_vs_timing_split below for the resulting engine-representability adjudication, kept explicitly separate from this historical-continuity finding, which is unchanged.

arithmetic_vs_timing_split._read_me_first: This item's historical continuity evidence (above) supports a single historical claim - the ATK/DEF result table - but that claim has TWO epistemically distinct engine-facing questions bundled in casual prose by an earlier pass: whether the pinned engine reproduces the ARITHMETIC/destruction result, and whether it reproduces a historically-distinctive DAMAGE-STEP TIMING/response-window procedure. These have different evidence and different engine status and must not be conflated - only the first is evidenced; the second is not, and is not used to justify anything.

adversarial_review_2026_08_29._read_me_first: An independent adversarial reviewer was asked to argue AGAINST retaining each of the three behaviours as an unconditional blocker, per this session's task instructions. Findings below; the adjudicator's response to each follows.

deck_out.challenge: Two agreeing dated documents (1999-02-04, 1999-05-05) prove 90 days of stability, not the remaining ~113 days to Tokyo Dome; the upper-bound sources (Japanese wiki, yugioh-history.com) are treated more skeptically elsewhere in this packet (restriction-list section) than here, an inconsistency; Ito Akira's tweet, though factually wrong about 'draw', may still indicate genuine period confusion about this exact rule.
deck_out.adjudication: RETAINED. The residual gap is real and is exactly why later_pre_tokyo_dome stays SUPPORTED_BUT_INCOMPLETE, not PROVEN - the challenge does not identify anything that would lower it further than that. The 'inconsistency' does not hold on inspection: the restriction-list section's skepticism targets one specific, already-flagged disputed sub-claim (scope), not a blanket rejection of the site's reliability; here the claim is independently stated by two editorially-separate sources. Ito Akira's tweet is about a casual writers'-room conversation, not a citation of the codified rule, and is outweighed by two independently-dated official print publications that agree with each other.

trap_activation_frequency.challenge: The same 113-day-gap argument as deck_out applies. More sharply: the upper-bound evidence (Quick-Play Spell Cards, Magic Ruler) and deck_out's upper-bound evidence (New Expert Rule, also Magic Ruler) may be two facets of the SAME single rules-overhaul release rather than two independently corroborating findings - risk of double-counting one data point as two.
trap_activation_frequency.adjudication: RETAINED, but the provenance-root risk is real and is now recorded explicitly (upper_bound_provenance_root, shared with deck_out) so it is never miscounted as independent corroboration. This does not weaken the CORE finding, which does not depend on the upper bound at all: PROVEN at Starter Box + independently re-documented 1999-05-05 (unrelated to Magic Ruler) + Expert Rules (the one documented intervening change) confirmed not to touch it. The upper bound is corroborating context, not the primary basis.

battle_calculation.challenge: Reviewer found this the WEAKEST case for downgrading: no source documents the recoil arithmetic ever changing, even decades later, making the 113-day interpolation safer than for the other two. The reviewer located the genuine vulnerability on the ENGINE side instead - NOT_REPRESENTABLE was not empirically verified this session (pinned ocgcore unavailable), and the recoil arithmetic may already match modern rules exactly.
battle_calculation.adjudication: RETAINED on historical-persistence grounds, which the adversarial review itself confirms is the strongest of the three. The engine-side caveat was already flagged (positive_continuity_evidence.items.battle_calculation.upper_bound_evidence) before this review; the review corroborates it as the real open question, not the historical continuity finding.

adversarial_review_2026_08_29.chaos_disruption_cross_check: Reviewer noted Tokyo Dome's documented severe disruption (near-riot conditions, cancelled finals) could let an overwhelmed volunteer judge deviate from either printed ruleset on judgment-call rules (deck-out, Trap-only responses) under pressure - a rule-specific mechanism, not the general 'which ruleset applied' uncertainty already priced into every matrix row's UNKNOWN tokyo_dome tier. Applied generally this argument would swallow all 21 matrix rows and is not specific enough on its own to earn extra weight beyond what UNKNOWN already reflects; noted as a residual acknowledged uncertainty, not a reason to downgrade.
